C. Induction of CYP2E1 by isoniazid leading to decreased serum levels of progesterone
D. Interference with the intestinal absorption of the oral contraceptive by pyrazinamide

The question discusses a situation where a young woman experienced contraceptive failure due to an interaction with anti-tuberculosis medication. The options provided list various mechanisms by which anti-TB drugs may impact the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. The correct answer is option A, "Induction of CYP3A4 by rifampin leading to decreased serum levels of ethinylestradiol and progesterone."

Rifampin is known to be a potent inducer of the cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) enzyme. This induction can lead to increased metabolism of oral contraceptives containing ethinylestradiol and progesterone, resulting in decreased serum levels and reduced contraceptive efficacy. Therefore, option A accurately describes the mechanism by which rifampin reduces the effectiveness of oral contraceptives.
